headline: High-risk write/egress pair: Plandex can modify files and use broad network egress, while mem0 has no documented isolation or ingestion controls for shared outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plandex can read/write project files and uses stdin/stdout plus a plan-local sandbox, so mem0 outputs could be fed back as trusted content if manually bridged. mem0 has no documented shared-channel protections or provenance tracking. This is not provably automatic, but the shared file/workflow path is plausible.
conditions: IF mem0 outputs are copied into Plandex project files or stdin/stdout
IF Plandex treats those files as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep mem0 outputs out of Plandex input files
Require a human review step before Plandex consumes mem0 text
Prefix mem0 outputs with explicit non-instruction markers
Disable any auto-apply workflow for imported text
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plandex has broad network egress and reads/writes the project directory, so any sensitive content that mem0 stores or emits into shared files can be transmitted to external model providers. mem0 itself shows no network egress, but the pair still creates a leakage path through Plandex's default external calls.
conditions: IF mem0 stores secrets or private notes in files Plandex reads
IF Plandex sends those file contents to its model provider or Plandex Cloud
mitigations: Do not place secrets in the shared project directory
Use a redaction pass before Plandex reads mem0 output
Restrict Plandex to a local/self-hosted model endpoint
Review outbound requests for sensitive payloads
requires-engineering: isolate the agents onto separate workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plandex can write the filesystem and modify git state, while mem0 is a knowledge-management agent that may also persist state through its own storage path even though that path is not documented here. Because both agents can plausibly touch shared mutable resources and Plandex supports multiple instances via shared backend state, concurrent writes can corrupt work or git history.
conditions: IF both agents target the same working tree or git repository
IF mem0 persists memory into files that Plandex also edits
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Serialize writes with a manual lock file
Avoid running Plandex auto-apply on shared repos
Commit after each agent finishes, not concurrently
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex is a planner with review-then-apply and optional auto-apply, so mem0-generated text can become actionable input if the operator routes it into Plandex plans. mem0 does not verify downstream actions, and Plandex can execute shell commands, making unverified propagation a realistic default workflow risk rather than a guaranteed failure.
conditions: IF mem0 output is used as source material for a Plandex plan
IF Plandex auto-apply is enabled or the operator approves actions without verification
mitigations: Require source citations before Plandex acts on mem0 output
Turn off auto-apply for plans derived from mem0
Have a human verify any commands before execution
Limit Plandex to drafting only, not execution
requires-engineering: add validation gates between planning and apply

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for mem0, while Plandex explicitly handles model provider API keys and can send data to Plandex Cloud or a self-hosted server. The compliance risk is therefore limited to configuration choices and is not provably a default breach from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Plandex inputs
IF Plandex is configured to use a non-compliant cloud or retention policy
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared prompts
Use a self-hosted Plandex deployment
Review retention settings before use
Document data classes allowed in the workflow
requires-engineering: obtain a DPA or compliance review
